newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends slightly weaker in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends slightly weaker in late trading.

text.p: LME three months copper closed a touch weaker in late inter-office trading on Thursday after abandoning earlier attempts to break the $2,300 a tonne barrier.
The market saw a bout of profit-taking after copper rallied to score an intraday high of $2,295 but then lost upside momentum, analysts said.
At 1900 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,270/2,273 after finishing the afternoon kerb up $25 at at $2,275.
Technical analysts said indicators were trending higher in support as the market looked to challenge resistance towards the recent high of $2,292, with the next upside target placed at $2,313.

Zinc was quieter after its earlier rally when it gained three percent on the day after fund buying propelled it above $1,200 in the morning and triggered more buy stops. It was last indicated at $1,222/1,226.
